title.en: Blueprint: watermill with a turning wheel

summary: A two-storey stone-and-timber mill with an overshot wheel on a wheel socket, a launder feeding it, a first-floor loading door under a hoist beam, and an animate(dt) that turns only the wheel.
objective: Seen from about eleven metres the mill reads as three tiers: wheel and launder breaking the gable, then rims, spokes, paddles and frame timbers, then hub bolts, rim straps and sill drips.
intent_signals: village mill with a turning wheel
example_prompts: Put a watermill on the stream at the edge of the village.
I need a mill whose wheel actually turns in the render loop.
not_for: Any claim about the gearing, head or power output of a real mill.
Hydraulic or structural simulation of a water wheel.

silhouette: 3.2 m wheel hanging clear of the +X gable and breaking the building outline from every angle
launder crossing above the wheel on two trestles, with a spilling lip over the crown
hoist beam projecting 1.3 m from the gable below the ridge at 6.83 m
medium: two wooden rims with an iron strap inside each, seven pairs of radial spokes and fourteen paddles running the full 84 cm width between the rims
stone ground storey and plastered timber upper storey divided by a projecting string course
four frame posts per upper long wall standing 7 cm proud, with top plate, sill beam and corner braces
first-floor loading door recessed 10 cm in its reveal directly under the hoist beam
fine: bright iron bolt heads at every spoke root, 8 cm across, on the outer rim face
hexagonal peg heads at the frame joints and clenched nail heads on the door leaves
sill drip groove under each window, a 2.4 cm shadow line below the sill lip
each paddle darkened by a different seeded amount, so the wet side of the wheel varies

principles: A mill is a machine with a house attached: model the wheel first and let the building be what carries it.
The wheel must be structurally believable at rest, not only in motion. Rims, spokes and a real axle read even in a still frame.
Animation belongs to one named group. animate(dt) turns the hub and nothing else, so the mill can stand still without falling apart.
implementation: Call create({ width, depth, wheelRadius, paddles, roofPitchDeg, speedRadPerSec, seed }); the returned object carries animate(dt).
Call animate(dt) once per frame with seconds; it returns false for dt <= 0 so a paused loop reports no motion.
Attach a millpond, sluice or sign through the named sockets; the wheel socket sits on the axle centre with an outward +X normal.
observable_checks: Run scripts/kit-proof.py and count features in close.png: at least two from each detail-ladder band must be visible in the frame.
animate(0) returns false and moves nothing; animate(0.016) returns true and rotates only the wheel group.
Two instances with different seeds vary the paddle shading and the frame posts while keeping the same wheel diameter.

known_limits: Authored creative geometry. Nothing here is a measurement of any real mill, drive train or material.
The poly budget is the triangle count observed at default parameters; 24 paddles costs about 10800 triangles.
footprint_m is the nominal house plan. The built bounding box is 9.4 x 5.3 m because the wheel, the launder and the eaves project past it.
The wheel turns at a constant rate. There is no water, no torque and no relationship between speedRadPerSec and any flow.
Tuned against ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0 with no post-processing.
creative_affordances: Any parameter may be pushed outside its stated range; the range is the band that was proved, not a limit.
Set speedRadPerSec to 0 for a derelict mill, or swap the roof and stone colours to move it to a different look.

defaults.rationale: A 1.6 m wheel radius puts the axle at 1.92 m, so the wheel fills the gable without passing the eave, and 14 paddles at that radius give a 70 cm pitch that still reads as separate blades at the far proof distance.
